prompt:
A car traveling at 15 m/s begins braking with a constant deceleration of $3 \text{ m/s}^2$.

**(a)** Calculate the time it takes for the car to come to a complete stop.

**(b)** Calculate the distance the car travels while braking.

**(c)** Verify your answer to (b) using a different kinematic equation than the one you used to derive it.

rubric.description: Correctly sets up v=v0+at with v=0 and solves for t=5 s
Correctly uses a kinematic equation (e.g. x=v0t+(1/2)at^2 with a=-3) to find the stopping distance
Correctly computes the stopping distance as 37.5 m
Correctly re-derives 37.5 m using a second, different kinematic equation (e.g. v^2=v0^2+2aΔx)

prompt:
A ball rolls off the edge of a cliff of height 78.4 m with a horizontal velocity of 15 m/s ($g = 9.8 \text{ m/s}^2$).

**(a)** Calculate the time it takes the ball to reach the ground.

**(b)** Calculate the horizontal distance (range) the ball travels before landing.

**(c)** Calculate the vertical component of the ball's velocity the instant before it lands.

rubric.description: Correctly uses h=(1/2)gt^2 (vertical motion only) to find t=4 s
Correctly computes the horizontal range using x=v0x·t
Correctly finds the range to be 60 m
Correctly computes the vertical velocity at impact as vy=gt=39.2 m/s

sampleResponse:
(a) The fall time depends only on vertical motion: h=(1/2)gt^2, so 78.4=(0.5)(9.8)t^2, t^2=16, t=4 s.
(b) Horizontal motion is at constant velocity: x = v0x·t = (15)(4) = 60 m.
(c) vy = gt = (9.8)(4) = 39.2 m/s.

prompt:
The velocity-time graph below shows an object's motion from t=0 to t=6 s.

**(a)** Calculate the object's acceleration between t=0 s and t=3 s.

**(b)** Calculate the object's total displacement between t=0 s and t=6 s.

**(c)** Describe, in words, what the object is doing between t=3 s and t=6 s.

rubric.description: Correctly computes acceleration between t=0 and t=3s as (12-0)/3 = 4 m/s^2
Correctly computes the total area under the graph (triangle from 0-3s plus rectangle from 3-6s)
Correctly finds the total displacement to be 54 m
Correctly describes the object as moving at a constant velocity of 12 m/s (zero acceleration) between t=3s and t=6s

sampleResponse:
(a) Acceleration = slope = (12-0)/(3-0) = 4 m/s^2.
(b) Displacement = area under the graph = triangle (0 to 3s: (1/2)(3)(12)=18 m) + rectangle (3 to 6s: (3)(12)=36 m) = 54 m.
(c) Between t=3s and t=6s, the graph is flat at v=12 m/s, meaning the object moves at a constant velocity of 12 m/s (zero acceleration) during this interval.

diagram.altText: Velocity-time graph rising from 0 to 12 meters per second between t=0 and t=3 seconds, then flat at 12 meters per second from t=3 to t=6 seconds
